lifecycleNotes: Replaces the WCF duplex callback: the client initiates the stream, so the server can no longer dial back to an idle client.
Events are ordered per order_id; the client deduplicates by occurred_at after a reconnect.
The server applies backpressure by awaiting the response writer; a persistently slow client terminates with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
Client disconnect cancels the CancellationToken and releases the subscription; there is no WCF session to resume.

sections.design: .NET 10 LTS with Grpc.AspNetCore on the server and Grpc.Net.Client for .NET consumers; code generation runs through the Grpc.Tools MSBuild integration so generated code is never checked in.

The Windows Service host is replaced by a modern .NET host on Kestrel serving HTTP/2 over TLS on 8443, with a separate HTTP/1.1 port for health and metrics. IIS is not used because it cannot serve gRPC reliably.

IOrderService becomes one gRPC service, contoso.orders.v1.OrderService, in one deployment unit. PerSession instancing is replaced by stateless scoped services plus a distributed subscription registry keyed by order_id, so no client affinity is required and duplex session state disappears.

Package contoso.orders.v1 lives in src/Contoso.Orders.Grpc/Protos/order_service_v1.proto and shared types in src/Contoso.Contracts.Protos/common_v1.proto (contoso.common.v1). Field numbers are assigned once, removed fields stay reserved by number and name, 19000-19999 is forbidden, and a breaking change requires contoso.orders.v2 registered alongside v1. A single integration owner holds all shared proto files.

decimal maps to contoso.common.v1.DecimalValue (int64 units plus int32 nanos); DateTime and DateTimeOffset map to google.protobuf.Timestamp in UTC and TimeSpan to Duration; Guid maps to a canonical lowercase string; enums gain an _UNSPECIFIED zero member and unknown values are surfaced; nullable values use proto3 optional; collections map to repeated or map with null and empty treated identically.

Typed faults map to gRPC status codes with google.rpc.Status details: OrderValidationFault to INVALID_ARGUMENT with OrderValidationDetail, missing entities to NOT_FOUND, authorization failures to PERMISSION_DENIED, and unexpected failures to INTERNAL with a correlation id only. A server interceptor replaces IErrorHandler and guarantees that no exception text, stack trace, or secret leaves the process.

wsHttpBinding message security is replaced by TLS 1.3 transport security with OIDC bearer tokens issued by the corporate identity provider; certificates are provisioned from the platform secret store by reference and rotated automatically. Message-level signing and WS-* headers have no gRPC equivalent and are dropped deliberately.

.NET authorization replaces PrincipalPermission: the default policy denies unauthenticated calls, orders.write guards SubmitOrder, orders.read guards SubscribeOrderStatus, and per-order data scoping is enforced in the service implementation and proved by tests.

WCF timeouts become client deadlines (30s for unary calls) with server-side CancellationToken propagation. SubmitOrder is idempotent by idempotency_key and may be retried on UNAVAILABLE and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED with exponential backoff and at most three attempts; streaming calls are not retried automatically. The service declares no one-way operations, so no acknowledged-delivery redesign is required.

OpenTelemetry traces and metrics for server and client replace WCF message inspectors and diagnostic tracing; structured logs carry a correlation id propagated in request metadata; RPC rate, error, duration, and payload size are recorded per method for parity comparison, and payload logging is redacted by default.

The standard grpc.health.v1.Health service reports per-service status; readiness probes the orders database and the identity provider, liveness stays process-local, and shutdown drains in-flight unary calls and closes status streams with OK before the host exits.

The service deploys as a container behind an HTTP/2-aware load balancer with client-side load balancing for internal callers; TLS material comes from the platform secret store; rollout is canary with automatic rollback on error-rate regression; no database migration is required for the pilot slice, so both stacks read and write the same additive schema.

WCF retirement requires every in-scope operation validated by the parity stage; zero legacy traffic for 14 consecutive days measured at the host; every consumer cut over or waived by an approved decision; rollback rehearsed; alerts, dashboards, and runbooks accepted; coexistence components removed or given a dated removal plan; and explicit human approval of the retirement decision. No gate may be satisfied by static analysis.

targetArchitecture.summary: A single stateless gRPC service on .NET 10 replaces the WCF order host. The duplex status callback becomes a server-streaming RPC, decimal totals use a shared DecimalValue message, and message-level WS-* security is replaced by TLS plus OIDC bearer tokens. The WCF endpoint stays routable for external partners until their cutover decision is approved.
